intended_object: The least positive natural number n satisfying a decidable predicate p (given that one exists), bundled with proofs that p n holds and that no smaller m satisfies p. The source is the docstring "PNat version of Nat.findX".
explanation: The body applies Nat.findX to the predicate on ℕ "n' is the coercion of some n : ℕ+ with p n". The resulting least witness is positive, so it lifts back to ℕ+, and it satisfies p. Minimality transfers because any m : ℕ+ with m < n and p m would give the smaller ℕ-witness (m : ℕ). The output type is exactly {n // p n ∧ ∀ m < n, ¬p m}, which is the least-element (well-ordering) specification on ℕ+. Restricting to ℕ+ is intentional: this is the ℕ+ analogue of Nat.findX, so it is not too narrow.
